articleTitle: Magnetic Skyrmions Based One-Bit Comparator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: This paper proposes a skyrmion based 1-bit comparator implemented using a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1\times 4$</tex> demultiplexer (DMUX) and an OR-gate. A stack is composed of heavy metal (HM) and ultrathin ferromagnetic (FM) i.e., platinum (Pt) and cobalt (Co), respec-tively. The stack can exhibit a large interfacial Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction (DMI), and the FM-HM interface can host stable, Néel-skyrmions at room temperature. The irradiation reduces the local anisotropy and DMI. The nonirradiated regions of the FM act as a potential barrier for skyrmions due to higher anisotropy. The proposed comparator is validated through micromagnetic simulations.

articleTitle: Modular Implementation of Directory-Based Cache Coherence for Multicore Processing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: Modern CPU designs are shifting toward multi-core architectures, as many commercial and scientific workloads benefit significantly from concurrent and multithreaded operations. This leads to increased throughput, performance, and efficiency. The cache coherence protocols are used for communication and coordination in multi-core - to achieve this gain. In the open-source environment, particularly in CVA6, the lack of a coherence-enabled cache controller motivates the need for a modular approach to enable multicore processing using CVA6. To overcome this limitation, we propose an invalidation-based directory protocol to enable cache coherency in multi-core shared memory Network-on-Chip (NoC) architecture.

articleTitle: Electrical Analysis of Stretchable Serpentine Interconnect for Flexible Electronic System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: Flexible electronics (FE) have a broad range of potential applications in healthcare monitoring and human-machine interactions due to their stretchability and conformability. The FE system comprises of devices (sensors) and interconnects. However, many times interconnect have been realized as rigid off board metallic interconnects. This creates high strain concentration in brittle metallic interconnects during the extensive mechanical stretching of FE systems. One of the critical parameters of the stretchable interconnect is geometry design. Therefore, special geometry designs are required to achieve high stretchability without creating high strains. While much research has focused on enhancing the stretchability of FE systems, the intrinsic electrical properties of different geometries have often been overlooked. In present work, two geometries are considered for interconnect viz. serpentine (Sp) and horseshoe (Hr). Further, in this manuscript, the electrical performance of stretchable interconnects is performed under systematically applied mechanical constraints using finite element simulative analysis. The analytical and ANSYS simulation results are obtained. Finally, the optimum performance comparison is drawn from the considered interconnect geometries. The developed advancements pave the way for creating FE systems that improve flexibility, safety, and functionality in various fields, such as healthcare monitoring, wearable technology and biomedical applications.

articleTitle: A 1024-Input Multi-Stage Voltage-Mode WTA Circuit for Selective Attention Based Processing in Massive Parallel Sensing Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: This work presents a high-speed high-resolution 1024-input voltage-mode WTA circuit which is suitable for selective attention based processing systems. The circuit uses multi-stage WTAs to improve the resolution and speed. The WTA blocks use a max selector circuit to ensure error-free comparisons in their succeeding stages. The outputs of the max selector circuits are buffered to reduce the delay due to the cascaded transmission gates. The 1024-input WTA circuit designed in UMC 180 nm CMOS process experiences a worst-case delay of 235 ns for an input resolution of 8 mV.

articleTitle: Consequence of Various Clock Parameters on Power / Timing Analysis for VLSI Circuits
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: Clock signals are pivotal in digital circuitry, syn-chronizing the operation of millions of transistors to achieve efficient and reliable performance. However, optimizing clock parameters is crucial for balancing power consumption and ensuring timing integrity in modern integrated circuits (ICs). This paper explores the impact of essential clock parameters such as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$r$</tex>ise/fall times, setup/hold times, skew, duty cycle, and latency on power consumption and timing analysis. With unchanged frequency, the synthesis result shows the impressive power and timing requirements optimization. Understanding and optimizing these clock parameters are essential for enhancing the overall performance and energy efficiency of digital 1Cs, paving the way for future advancements in circuit design and implementation.

articleTitle: Deep Learning for Brain Tumor Detection with FPGA Pathway
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: Brain tumors, particularly gliomas, present significant challenges in medical science because of their high incidence, recurrence, and mortality rates. Perfect diagnosis using Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) is crucial. Recent developement in deep learning, particularly in Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and transfer learning models, have significantly enhanced the automation and accuracy of medical image analysis. This work proposes a comprehensive framework for classification of brain tumor using MRI data, integrating CNN, VGG16, and EfficientNetB0 models with a Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) implementation pathway. Our approach enhances the models' resilience and applicability using robust data augmentation methods, including geometrical transformation. Experimental results demonstrate that both CNN and EfficientNetB0 achieve classification accuracies exceeding 90%, showcasing their effectiveness in distinguishing between gliomas, meningiomas, and pituitary tumors. The FPGA-based accelerator significantly improves processing efficiency. This framework advances tumor classification and addresses computational challenges, paving the way for practical applications in medical diagnostics.

articleTitle: A Fully Digital Rail-to-Rail Low Power Dynamic Comparator for Smart Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: A low supply voltage, low power, rail-to-rail dynamic comparator using digital gates is proposed in this work. The design takes advantage of digital gates, which allows transistors to operate in deep sub-threshold regions at very low power supply. The proposed design uses three cascaded stages of 2-input NAND and 2-input NOR arranged in a complementary manner to provide rail-to-rail common mode range. The purpose of cascaded structure is to minimize the offset and latency by enhancing the transconductance of the input stage. The design is implemented in UMC 65 nm CMOS technology at 100 KHz operating frequency. The simulation is performed for different supply voltages starting from 500 mV down to 150 mV. The worst-case latency of 5.3 μs is observed at 150 mV supply, while consuming 18 nW of power. Moreover, Monte-Carlo simulations are performed for 1000 runs and the offset standard deviation of 7.5 mV is observed for 150 mV supply voltage.

articleTitle: You Only Look Once in Dark: An Analytical Approach for Low Light Object Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: In recent decades, object detection has been one of the most significant areas of research, which enables an autonomous machine to make intelligent decisions without any human intervention. Low-light object detection faces numerous challenges including noise, granules, and ambiguity in no or limited color information. Single Shot Detectors (SSD), especially, You-Only-Look-Once (YOLO) one of the latest improvised object detection techniques, find objects within the image in a single forward pass instead of separating into two stages like Faster R-CNN by identifying regions of interest. This paper conducts an extensive analysis of the performances of the latest ML-mediated object detection technique, YOLO. All the versions of YOLO are evaluated based on various ranges of lux value in an experimented environment. The main focus of the research work is to compute the performances of YOLO techniques in varying light conditions starting from bright to low-light and darkest environments. The analysis presents a compatible result within a considerable threshold between low and high lux values <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\text{lumen}/m^{2})$</tex>. The real-world experiment is established on a standard dataset, COCO, under varying light-conditioned setups where the vision system frequently transits from brighter to darker or vice versa. The experimental computation reveals the chronological performance order: YOLO v8<YOLO v3< YOLO v4< YOLO vS<YOLO v6< YOLO v7< YOLO v9 in performance superiority from best higher to lower lux ranges, at the given experimental scenarios. YOLO v9 has been found to be efficient at 90% detection rates respectively for detecting objects at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$210-600 \ \ \text{lm/m}^2$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$30-210\ \ \ 1\mathrm{m}/ {m}^{2}$</tex> lux values in consecutive brighter and darker environments. A dynamic Decision Support System(DSS) has been introduced that confirms a balanced performance of object detection in varying light conditions.

articleTitle: Design of an Operational Transconductance Amplifier-Based Charge Pump for Phase-Locked Loop Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: This paper presents a charge pump (CP) that includes an operational transconductance amplifier (OTA) with improved power efficiency, making it suitable for low-power applications. The 90nm CMOS process technology is used to simulate the proposed OTA and CP architecture, with an input voltage of 1.2 V. The suggested CP operates at a power consumption of 78.01 µW and exhibits phase noise, reference spur, and output noise levels of -123.6 dBc/Hz, - 115.50 dBc/Hz, and -161.5 dB, respectively. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed charge pump exhibits a locking time of just 18 ns, which is significantly faster than previous CP circuits. Additionally, the charge pump has a current mismatch of only 0.06%.

articleTitle: A GUI Based Digital IC Tester
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: The primary objective of our developed Digital Inte-grated Circuit(IC) tester is to create an efficient and user-friendly Digital Integrated Circuit testing solution. It has been specially designed for educational institutes' electronic laboratories. The novelty of the product lies in the user-friendly Graphical User Interface(GUI) and capability to test each functional block of a digital IC, displaying the pin diagram and truth table. An indi-vidual functional block's working status allows the user/student to use the other available working blocks of the same IC and thus also helps reduce the e-waste due to ICs. The availability of the truth table and pin diagram helps the students get an easy and better learning experience. The testing results show that the tester is highly accurate.

articleTitle: Temperature Sensing Readout Circuits with 4H-SiC Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: 4H-Silicon Carbide (4H-SiC) technology is well known for its superior thermal conductivity, high-temperature stability, and robustness in harsh environments. This paper presents three distinct temperature-sensing readout circuits (a PMOS array, an NMOS array, and a CMOS-based ring os-cilia tor) utilizing this technology. The readout circuits with PMOS and NMOS arrays are showing Proportional to Absolute Temperature (PTAT) behavior. For a temperature range of 25–200 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${}^{\circ} C$</tex>, these designs are showing a sensitivity of 26.8 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$mV/{}^{\circ} C$</tex> (PMOS array) and 19.60 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$mV/^{\circ} C$</tex> (NMOS array), respectively, at a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V_{DD}$</tex> of 20 V. At the same power supply voltage a 7-stage CMOS ring oscillator-based sensor which gives the digital output, is showing a sensitivity of 44.01 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$kHz/{}^{\circ} C$</tex> and a power consumption of 2.14 m W. These readout circuits find potential applications in implementing on-chip temperature sensing systems.

articleTitle: Design and Development of VariScan: A Continuous Heart Rate Variability Monitor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: Heart Rate Variability is a widely studied physiological marker that reflects the autonomic regulation of the heart. HRV represents the autonomic nervous system's control over the heart and is crucial for cardiovascular health monitoring. Heart Rate Variability is measured using methodologies such as electrocardiography (ECG) for RR interval analysis and spectral decomposition, and photoplethysmography (PPG) for blood volume changes. Some of the existing methods use mobile health (mHealth) apps with smartphone sensors, and time-frequency analysis for comprehensive HRV dynamics assessment across various time scales. This paper presents VariScan, a device designed to provide accurate and continuous(24x7) HRV monitoring using the MAX30102 sensor with an IoT controller for data transmission. The suggested module in this paper is a low-cost non-invasive device, which can be customized and easily calibarated based on the user applications. VariScan was tested on 10 subjects to predict the HR at five different time instants, and the marked reading was compared with an available heart rate meter. The device HR readings were within 0.5 per cent of the accuracy.

articleTitle: Exploring the Application of Variable Frequency Clock as the Constituent of OCT
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: Swept-source Optical Coherence Tomography (SS-OCT) has become the benchmark for clinical ocular imaging. In recent SS-OCT systems, a sampling clock ‘k-Clock’ is used to sample the interference signal. The ‘k-Clock’ doesn't have a fixed frequency; its frequency varies according to the frequency of the interference signal. The generation of the ‘k-Clock’ is quite complex and involves bulky analog components. This could potentially degrade the sampling quality, add complexity, and increase the cost of the OCT engine. As per the literature survey, it can be inferred that a Variable Frequency Clock (VFC) could be a potential solution, where an all-digital system inside the OCT engine can produce a particular pattern of VFC spectrum comprising all the required frequencies needed for the efficient sampling of the interference signal. Through this work, a system design is targeted to generate the VFC spectrum with multiple frequency changeovers over equal stay time (Tfreq) for each frequency on the spectrum.

articleTitle: A 72 mW, 50 MHz Bandwidth Low-IF CMOS Receiver Front End with Improved Linearity and Dynamic Range
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: The design of receiver frontend using CMOS technology has been a challenge for long distance communication due to low value of received RF input power and noise associated with MOSFETs. In this paper, a CMOS receiver frontend architecture is proposed that can detect up to -95 dBm of RF input power levels while consuming a power of 72 mW. The two-stage low noise amplifier (LNA), mixer, filter and 4-stage variable gain amplifier (VGA) was integrated for detection of wide range of RF signals and to offer better dynamic range for receiver for further processing. The VGA was incorporated to amplify the weak signal of the filter output when low input RF power was received (-95 dBm). The noise figure of the receiver is found to be 2.45 dB with a 1 dB compression point value of -27 dB. The receiver design can be used for sub-6 GHz 5G wireless systems and Wireless LAN with a maximum bandwidth of 50 MHz.

articleTitle: Design of a Portable and Non-Invasive Hemoglobin Measuring Device
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: Detection of Anemia in early stages is very important for proper treatment and clinical trials. There is a dire need of point-of-care screening, early diagnosis and monitoring of Anemia but the laboratory based practices are mostly expensive and technically challenging for middle or low income countries where Anemia is majorly prevalent. The non-invasive measurement method of hemoglobin could be promising alternative as it needs no blood sample, and consequently it is with patient's comfort, minimum infection risk, free from repetitive change of chemicals, and one can monitor in real time. It would also help people staying in remote places through remote diagnostics. This paper presents a non-invasive approach based on transmission spectroscopy, where optical technique has been used to measure Hb concentration with higher accuracy. The proposed device has high potential to be valuable in diagnosis of anemia and its follow up.

articleTitle: VLSI Implementation of Edge Detection Chip: A Prospective Design
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: Edge detection is a basic function of image processing and a versatile application that includes object recognition, surveillance, and medicinal imagery. A suggested circuit improves the efficiency and flexibility of the edge detection techniques by defining its behavior using Verilog, a language for describing hardware.This paper describes the design and implementation of an edge detection circuit using a 4-bit carry look ahead adder and a 2's complement circuit for handling the negative bit,using the Verilog programming languages.Improved computing speed and accuracy are achieved by the circuit by integrating a carry Look Ahead adder and a 4-bit multiply. This paper represents the circuit design step of Verilog Code, hardware synthesis, and algorithm. Performance analysis represents how well the suggested approach works for reliability and quickly identifying edges. This research presents the possibility of hardware acceleration for real-time applications and advances edge detection approaches in digital image processing. To illustrate the results, the suggested design was simulated using Verilog coding. For the purpose of estimation of VLSI parameters, it was then synthesized in Vivado (xc7vx48Stffg1157-1). The perspective insights and future motivation ideas to create energy-efficient VLSI solutions for the edge detection convolution technique are provided by this implementation result.

articleTitle: Power, Performance and Area Optimization of Asynchronous FIFO
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: This paper focuses on the power, performance, and area (PPA) analysis and physical implementation of power-sensitive asynchronous first-in-first-out (FIFO), offering two novel solutions to improve power efficiency. One productive scheme to reduce an asynchronous FIFO architecture's power usage is by power gating in RTL level, another streamlined approach is the application of synthesis iSpatial flow, which unifies physical optimization for better predictability of the proposed design and its PPA evaluation. It uses accurate timing information post-placement and clock tree synthesis, thus introduces powerful logic restructuring and enabling a more power and area-efficient timing closure methodology. Power gating scheme reduces leakage power by more than 30% compared to conventional asynchronous FIFO. iSpatial flow reduces the leakage power of about 50% on the proposed power gated asynchronous FIFO.

articleTitle: Efficient Framework with Sparse Acquisition in CMOS Image Sensors for Low-Power Edge Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: Memory bandwidth and power consumption is of utmost importance in the design of low power edge devices. This makes it essential to conserve power both at the sensor node and the computational unit. Our paper proposes a system design methodology to save power by acquiring compressed data at the CMOS Image Sensor (CIS) and making the Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models lightweight for edge applications. A detailed study highlights the effect of sensor directed sparsity at the CIS, and its effect on CNN models such as VGG-16, MobileNet, ResNet50, EfficientNet, and ResNext models. It provides empirical evidence that the performance is mostly maintained even after pruning and quantization of considered models. The imagenette dataset is used to curate the data with the proposed acquisition pipeline that introduces data sparsity, and the experimental results provide evidence that the proposed pipeline performs at par with conventional CIS acquisition mode. For example, the analysis of VGG-16 model for a sparsity threshold level of 0.2 shows compression of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times 7.6, \times 16$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times 61$</tex> using only pruning (P), only quantization (Q), and with both pruning+quantization (P+Q), respectively. It is also observed that the proposed acquisition pipeline can achieve significant parameter reduction through pruning for model compression, comparable to convectional pipeline.

articleTitle: Fortified-SoC: A Novel Approach Towards Trojan Resilient System-on-Chip Design
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: This research paper investigates a hardware-type attack on System-on-Chips (SoCs) involving a trigger and a payload. A stealthy and controllable fabrication time attack, A2, is demonstrated, and a circuit is developed based on charge accumulation from rare events within the system. When voltage gets buildup due to charge coupling, the payload has been activated, leading to a privilege-escalation attack. In this research, a specific analog hardware Trojan (A2) detection and mitigation circuit is designed. This Trojan affects the circuit performance by targeting sensitive wires (like reset) in SoCs. This paper presents a method for detecting the Trojan and implementing proper mitigation techniques to safeguard SoCs from malicious attacks.

articleTitle: Variation of Sensitivity of AlGaN/GaN High Electron Mobility Transistor(HEMT) Based Hydrogen Gas Sensor on Thickness of AlGaN and Mole Fraction of Aluminium
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: AlGaN/GaN High Electron Mobility Transistors (HEMTs) have attracted a lot of attention in gas sensing applications due to their special characteristics. These materials are suitable for sensing applications because of their wide band gap and high carrier mobility. The advantage of using AlGaN/GaN HEMTs for gas sensing is their high selectivity and sensitivity. An optimized HEMT structure for hydrogen gas sensing is presented in this work whose sensitivity value is high. This work also shows how the drain current varies in response to changes in the thickness of AlGaN and the mole fraction of Al in AlGaN. It is seen that as hydrogen gas is varied from Oppm to 10ppm the drain current increases. The simulations were performed at room temperature using Silvaco TCAD.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Based Algorithm for Shockley-Read-Hall Recombination and Augur Recombination Predictions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: In the realm of Very Large Scale Integration (VLSI) technology, accurate prediction of carrier recombination mechanisms is crucial for optimizing device performance and reliability. Shockley-Read-Hall (SRH) and Auger recombination are dominant mechanisms that influence carrier lifetimes and, consequently, the overall device behavior. Traditionally, Technology Computer-Aided Design (TCAD) tools have been employed to simulate carrier recombination processes; however, these methods are computationally expensive and require extensive parameter calibration, hindering efficient exploration of design spaces. This paper explores the potential of utilizing machine learning techniques to predict SRH and Auger recombination rates, offering a more efficient and versatile approach to VLSI device design and optimization. Our machine learning models predict these values with high accuracy and require much lower latency than the TCAD simulations.

articleTitle: Optimized Transfer Learning with CNNs for Superior COVID-19 Detection in Chest X-Ray Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: The “Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Corona Virus” (SARS-CoV2) causing COVID-19 has led to a global pandemic with significant fatalities. Researchers have used Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to improve diagnosis, but previous studies were hindered by limited and unbalanced datasets. Limited research has focused on large, balanced datasets, allowing for better accuracy in multi-class classification for COVID-19 detection. This research uses VGG19, ResNet50, DenseNet201, and CheXNet models to design a robust deep learning model for COVID-19 detection using chest X-ray images. Through significant experimentation, the convolutional base of these pre-trained models was frozen, and new fully connected layers were added. Hyperparameters such as dense layers, units per layer, learning rate, decay steps, decay rate, dropout rate, and epochs were meticulously optimized to evaluate the performance of the models at different parameters. The model VGG19 achieved 97.8% accuracy in multi-class classification, outperforming existing research using the same dataset.

articleTitle: FPGA Implementation of an Efficient FIR Filter Using Double MAC Unit
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: By enhancing the efficiency and throughput of FIR filters, significant improvements can be made in many digital signal processing applications across various domains, ranging from telecommunications and audio processing to biomedical signal analysis and beyond. This paper proposes an 8-bit FIR filter which leverages the capabilities of DSP48E2 elements within Xilinx UltraScale FPGA devices to achieve superior performance in terms of throughput and maximum clock frequency. The proposed filter was designed and implemented on a Kintex UltraScale+ XCKU3P FPGA using Xilinx Vivado 2018.3. The input and output data were streamed in and out using AXI4S streaming protocol and the design was verified using cocotb framework. Finally, the performance metrics such as resource utilization and maximum clock frequency were studied. The comparative analysis showed a remarkable efficiency improvement in the proposed FIR filter, with only half the number of DSP elements required for a given number of operations, coupled with a 1.5 x enhancement in maximum clock frequency compared to conventional FIR filters.

articleTitle: Proximity Detection Based Low-Cost and Handheld IoT Device for Tracking Lost Objects
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: This paper presents a novel device leveraging the ESP32 micro controller to determine the proximity of a Wi-Fi signal source such as a smartphone hotspot or Wi-Fi router based on the received signal strength indicator (RSSI) values. The device connects to a smartphone hotspot, monitors RSSI values, and provides audio feedback proportional to the distance from the signal source. The proposed implementation can be employed as a low-cost handheld device for locating a misplaced Wi-Fi enabled smart device and also as a proximity tracker for items like bags. This paper discusses the design, implementation and potential applications of the proposed system.

articleTitle: Efficient Motion Estimation for Video Compression Using Approximate Arithmetic in Sum of Absolute Difference Computation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: Designing power-efficient digital systems is essential, particularly for multimedia applications in mobile devices. This paper presents a novel approach to motion estimation in video compression by integrating imprecise Lower-part-OR adders (LOA) into the Sum of Absolute Difference (SAD) computation units. The primary contribution of this work lies in the first application of LOA specifically for motion estimation in High Effi-ciency Video Coding (HEVC). The proposed architecture achieves significant power savings of up to 11.5 %, while maintaining a minimal increase in BjØntegaard Delta Rate (BD- Rate) of just 0.47 % to 0.68 %, showing a negligible impact on video quality. The architecture supports variable block sizes and is scalable for real-time processing of high-definition video, synthesized using 45 nm standard cell technology. This combination of approximate arithmetic with scalable design for video compression represents a unique and practical contribution to the field, offering an optimal balance between power efficiency and video quality preservation.

articleTitle: A Hybrid CNN-BiLSTM Neural Network Architecture for Early Prediction of Parkinson's Disease
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: Parkinson's Disease (PD) is a gradually worsening neurological condition in which several neurons become impaired with aging. This impairment of neurons leads to a decrease in dopamine production, which is the primary cause of Parkinson's disease. PD impairs motor functions and hinders cognitive and emotional stability, noticeably degrading the patient's quality of life. While PD remains incurable, proper diagnosis, early detection, and timely medication can assist PD patients in their healthier aging. Electroencephalogram (EEG) signals represent the brain's electrical activity and provide critical insights into neural activities. Existing methods in deep learning necessitate manual feature extraction, which requires domain expertise. Hence, this work represents an automated hybrid CNN-BiLSTM neural network architecture that predicts Parkinson's disease using rest-EEG signals. First, we design three 1–D CNN layers to extract the spatiotemporal relationship across the EEG channels. Subsequently, we utilize BiLSTM to identify temporal characteristics relevant to classifying these spatiotemporal features. The study utilizes EEG recordings from two open-access datasets: the University of Mexico (UNM) EEGs and the University of California San Diego (UCSD) resting state EEGs. Our methods achieved values of 97.24%, 97.83%, 96.68%, and 96.56% of accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and precision, respectively, for the UNM dataset, whereas 98.3%,97.89%,98.70%,98.66% of accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, precision respectively for the UCSD dataset. The proposed model's performance is compared with the state-of-the-art techniques to showcase its superiority. We further show that the model responds to dopaminergic medication, capturing EEG changes induced by it.

articleTitle: A Hardware-Software Co-Design Approach to Implement PUFs and TRNGs on FPGAs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: Physically-unclonable-functions (PUFs) and true-random-number-generators (TRNGs) are extensively used in security and authentication applications. However, the different designs of PUFs and TRNGs must be validated for their practi-cality and quality. Field-programmable-gate-arrays (FPGAs) are cost-effective and time-saving alternatives to do so. The existing literature lacks a general methodology for implementing afore-mentioned designs on FPGAs, which makes the designers' task difficult, especially while providing comparisons with state-of-the-art designs. To solve these challenges, we propose a hardware-software co-design methodology tailored for implementing PUFs and TRNGs on FPGAs. PUFs exploit manufacturing variations to generate unique device fingerprints crucial for secure authen-tication and cryptographic key generation. Our implementation simplifies the process of testing and recording the responses of any new PUF or TRNG on Xilinx FPGAs. We have implemented Arbiter PUF, Ring PUF, and PDL-based TRNG on Zedboard (AES-Z7EV-7Z020-G). We further report metrics of uniformity, and reliability along with results from NIST randomness tests for TRNGs.

articleTitle: Event-Based Vision for Real-Time Speed Detection: A Low Resource Utilization Hardware-Software Co-Design Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: Event-based vision algorithms are gaining traction for applications such as object tracking, gesture recognition, and optical flow estimation due to their high temporal resolution and low power consumption. However, to derive meaningful information from the event, current algorithms either require significant hardware resources or specialized neuromorphic hardware, rendering them unsuitable for usage in resource-constrained IoT applications. This paper presents a hardware-software co-design approach for real-time speed detection using a conventional camera to emulate event-based data. The proposed solution includes an algorithm that processes serially captured images to generate events, followed by a lightweight algorithm for speed detection. The event generation is implemented on the software, while hardware Intellectual Property (IP) is designed for efficient speed calculation. Compared to existing methods, our approach enhances processing time by 69× with comparable accuracy, providing a cost-effective and low-power alternative for real-time speed detection in IoT environments.

articleTitle: Towards Harnessing the Potential of Compression and Encoding to Enhance NVM Lifespan
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: Non-volatile Memories (NVM) are considered as alternatives of the conventional DRAM-based main memories. However, slow and energy-intensive write operations as well as poor write endurance limit their chances of adoption as the main-stream main memory standard. In this paper, we have proposed a technique called CompDyEn that integrates compression with block encoding in a dynamic fashion. This two phase policy, first compresses the blocks based on BDI technique and then applies FNW encoding technique dynamically, depending on the size of the compressed block. It results in fine granularity encoding on top of compression and facilitates substantial reduction in bit-flips. CompDyEn achieves significant reduction in bit-flips over baseline which leads to eventual improvement in the NVM lifetime.

articleTitle: Word Level Sign Language Recognition Using MediaPipe and LSTM-GRU Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: Indian Sign Language (ISL) is crucial to carrying out smooth and effective communication between the deaf and the hard-of-hearing community and those who can hear clearly. This paper proposes a new approach for wordlevel Indian Sign Language recognition using the MediaPipe framework, aided by the Long-Short Term Memory (LSTM) and Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) network. Our approach uses robust hand and pose tracking features of MediaPipe to infer precise and comprehensive feature representations of sign gestures. These features are then fed into a hybrid LSTMG RU network designed to capture Temporal dependencies, improving recognition accuracy. We have tested the proposed system using a varied dataset. Experimental results indicate our approach outperforms current methods by large margins in recognition accuracy and processing system speed. The test accuracy achieved through this research is 89.50%, which is small but a definite improvement of 2.1% over existing models. The findings corroborate the potential of using state-of-the-art tracking frameworks with deep learning techniques to develop efficient and accurate ISL recognition systems.

articleTitle: Highly Reliable, Feed-Forward and Multi-Arbiter based Physical Unclonable Function for IoT security
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: As the Internet of Things (IoT) evolves, securing IoT-enabled devices has become crucial due to the risk of increased cyber-attacks. The cryptographic methods used traditionally are unsuitable for IoT nodes due to their limited resources. Physically Unclonable Functions offer a cost-effective solution by generating unique keys from the inherent random variations in integrated circuits through challenge-response pairs (CRPs). This paper introduces a novel PUF design based on feed-forward and multi-arbiter PUFs, it leverages process variations in arbiter circuits to produce unique CRPs, enhancing reliability by converting device delay variations into distinct digital outputs. Implementation using 180 nm CMOS technology show that the PUF achieved a uniformity of 48.09%, average bit-aliasing of 48%, inter-Hamming distance of 50%, and reliability of 97.14%. Each response bit consumes 0.68 mW of power, ensuring efficient performance across a wide temperature range from -40°C to 120°C, surpassing other arbiter-based PUF designs in efficiency.

articleTitle: An Algorithmic Approach of Generating a VFC of Low Average Frequency Ramp
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: With the rapid evolution of Integrated Chips (IC), the number of components housed on a single chip has already crossed a billion. The frequency needs of these components range from some MHz to a few GHz, necessitating numerous individual frequency synthesizers on the chip in order to generate the required frequency for these individual components. The absolute chip area and the power demanded by these synthesizers pose a problem in further scaling down of the technology. It is studied that an on-chip Variable Frequency Clock (VFC) can become a solution to the problem where a central system inside the chip can produce a particular pattern of VFC spectrum that ranges from low to high frequency, comprising of all the required frequencies of those individual components. Here, an algorithmic approach for system design is targeted that will be able to generate the VFC spectrum with multiple frequency changeovers (at least more than 8) over equal stay time <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(T_{freq})$</tex> for each frequency level on the spectrum to achieve a low average frequency ramp.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Multiuser Classification for Malicious User Detection in 5G and Beyond Cooperative Sensing Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: Cognitive radio (CR)-based 5G and beyond networks have emerged as a potential technology, offering secondary users (SUs) the ability to utilize radio spectrum designated for licensed primary users (PUs) in their absence. Cooperative spectrum sensing (CSS) plays a crucial role in enhancing spectrum sensing accuracy within CR networks. However, the efficacy of CSS can be undermined by potential attacks from malicious users (MUs) transmitting inaccurate sensing information to the fusion center (FC). This study introduces a novel machine learning (ML) based scheme for identifying malicious users in CR networks before their data reaches the FC, thereby enabling the complete insulation of FC from adversarial signals generated by malicious users. Through simulations, the effectiveness of the proposed deep neural network (DNN) algorithm-based ML approach in detecting MUs is evaluated. The proposed DNN model overcomes the existing schemes by classifying multiple SUs before reaching the FC.

articleTitle: A Novel Monocular Camera-based Modular Reference Generation for Autonomous Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: Autonomous driving technology is rapidly gaining traction in the market due to its inherent benefits, including improved safety, enhanced driver comfort, and more efficient transportation. This paper proposes a modular architecture for real-time assistance in autonomous driving vehicles utilizing a rule-based steering and speed reference generation. The reference generation module is designed to achieve primary features like obstacle handling and lane following. It follows an approach based on the first principles of computer vision and the funda-mental equations of motion. This approach thus eliminates the need for higher computational and memory usage, reduces power demand, and makes the decision-making process predictable and transparent. Finally, the algorithm is validated and verified experimentally.

articleTitle: 0.6 to 1.2V Wide Voltage Range Bandgap Reference Generator in 18nm UTBB-FD-SOI Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: This paper presents a CMOS bandgap reference (BGR) circuit, which can generate multiple reference voltages ranging from 0.6V to 1.2V. In this work, two topologies of the current mode BGR circuit are designed and compared with the existing reference voltage mode BGR circuit. All the topologies of the BGR circuit have been designed in 18nm FDSOI Technology. The optimized topology with the supply voltage of 1.8 V shows the temperature coefficient (TC) of 35-ppm/°C from -40 °C to 150 °C for the reference voltage of 600m V as well as 1.2V. The measured power supply rejection ratio (PSRR) is 76 dB from 1 Hz to 10 kHz: For the 10% variation in supply voltage (1.8V), the observed variation in Vref is 0.15%. The Monte-Carlo analysis shows the measured Vref is 600 ± 15 mV (3o) for 1000 samples.

articleTitle: Kalman Filter: A Crucial Step Towards the Development of NavIC
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: Navigation with Indian Constellation (NavIC) is an autonomous satellite system consisting of seven constellations, with three in geostationary orbit and four in geosynchronous orbit. Achieving precise positioning and velocity estimations under noisy conditions is crucial for applications such as vehicle guidance, disaster management, and transportation improvement. We propose a novel implementation of a Kalman Filter for processing NavIC satellite measurements, optimizing position, velocity, and timing estimations. The innovation in this filter design lies in its efficient noise reduction and high accuracy in estimations. Our design achieves a power consumption of 0.103 Wand an area of 84303.850 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu m^{2}$</tex>. To further enhance the design, we aim to incorporate clock gating and power gating techniques, reducing overall power consumption and making it highly suitable for low-power, real-time navigation applications.

articleTitle: Low IF CMOS Receiver with 3-Stage LNA for Sub-GHz Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: In this paper, the low-IF architecture for CMOS receiver is explored for narrow-band, long-range applications for the frequency band of 865–867 MHz. The challenges in the receiver design and integration issues of low noise amplifier, mixer, filter, variable gain amplifier, sample and hold circuit, 4 - bit analog to digital converter are discussed. The performance of receiver is optimized using UMC 180 nm CMOS technology and the tradeoff in the performance parameters is compiled in a single parameter i.e, Figure of Merit (FOM). The bandwidth that is used in this design is 1 MHz which is obtained after down conversion and in the filter output. The design is optimized to attain a power gain and noise figure of 33 dB and 2.5 dB at mixer stage. The dynamic range of 4-bit flash ADC is found to be 13 dB The receiver consumes 80 mW of power with a 1 dB compression point of -39 dBm input power. The results suggest that the proposed design can be used for all narrow-band and long-range sub-GHz communication.

articleTitle: SWIFT: Swarm Intelligence Driven ESL Synthesis for Functional Trojan Fortification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: This paper presents a novel Swarm Intelligence driven Electronic System-Level (ESL) synthesis-based security methodology for functional Trojan fortification (called ‘SWIFT’). Backdoor functional Trojan covertly inserted in the reusable hardware designs is a major concern for ensuring reliability functionality of consumer electronics (CE) systems and also for ensuring consumer trust. Erroneous computed output due to malicious functional Trojan can cause malfunctioning of such reusable IP cores. Therefore, the proposed methodology introduces a framework that integrates triple modular redundancy (TMR) along with a unique multi-vendor allocation that enables the generation of Trojan fortified (resistant) reusable hardware intellectual property (IP) designs capable of countering functional Trojan, if present and producing the correct output. The proposed approach integrates the swarm intelligence-based design space exploration (DSE) process with Trojan fortification design process to optimize any possible design overhead incurred due to TMR design. Results of the experimental evaluation prove that the proposed approach can generate low-cost Trojan fortified IP designs at meagre exploration time and at the expense of nominal overhead compared to prior work (that handle Trojan detection only). Further, the presented approach can handle a several potential vulnerabilities in the DSP design, which shows its robust security strength.

articleTitle: Power Reduction of a Level Triggered D Flip-Flop using Clock Gating and Power Gating Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: In modern digital design, energy efficiency is a major concern, especially for low-power applications. This paper investigates ways to reduce the power consumption of Level Triggered D-Flip-Flops (LT-DFFs) generated by the application of clock and power-gating techniques. Clock gates selectively disable clock signals in registers when their operation is not necessary, thereby reducing dynamic power consumption. On the other hand, the power strip completely isolates the circuit sections by disconnecting the power supply during the inactive period, minimizing leakage currents. This study explores the simulation and implementation of these technologies with industry standard design tools, evaluates their power reduction effectiveness, and maintains time and functional requirements. The experimental results show significant energy savings in the LT-DFF without compromising performance, highlighting the potential of time-saving and energy-saving strategies to improve energy efficiency of digital circuits. The Proposed Design - I and II demonstrate significant reduction in switching power, achieving a 40 % improvement when the input switches every 4 clock cycles or longer. All designs are operated at an operating frequency of 1 G Hz and input switches with a switching factor <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\alpha)$</tex> of 0.33.

articleTitle: iGLU 4.1: An Intelligent Framework of Diabetes Prediction using Glucose-Insulin Values and Physiological Parameters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: Nowadays, diabetes is a critical health issue for human beings. With the concern of being diabetic, people are more conscious of continuous glucose monitoring and medication. For this purpose, people are completely focused on smart monitoring devices, which can instantly measure glucose value without pain. However, the continuous glucose monitoring is not enough for diabetes prediction. Physiological parameters and other conditions are key factors that increase the likelihood of diabetes. Hence, it is required to propose a model, which predicts diabetes based upon the physiological parameters. In this paper, a machine learning-based diabetes prediction framework has been proposed, which evaluates the likelihood of diabetes based on diastolic blood pressure (DBP), body mass index (BMI), insulin intake, blood glucose value and skin thickness. The proposed framework has been calibrated using the DNN model. 543 subject observations have been taken to calibrate, validate and test the proposed DNN model. Overall 82% accuracy has been reported as a true prediction of diabetes. 0.0705 mean absolute error (MAE) has been observed in the predicted likelihood of diabetes using an optimized DNN model. The proposed iGLU 4.1 diabetes prediction paradigm helps the doctor diagnose and prescribe medication at remote locations.

articleTitle: HLS Based Hardware Watermarking Using IP Seller's Superimposed Facial Anthropometric Features
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: Ensuring the security of hardware intellectual property (IP) designs is crucial for IP sellers/vendors due to the exposure of the global design chain process to security risks like IP piracy and false IP ownership claim. A potential threat within system-on-chip (SoC) or foundry house may involve piracy or fraudulent claim of ownership rights by an attacker. Therefore, ensuring the security of IP designs is paramount from an IP seller's perspective. This paper presents a novel high level synthesis (HLS) based hardware watermarking by exploiting IP seller's superimposed facial anthropometric features as imperceptible embedded watermark. The watermark is embedded into the hardware IP design during HLS as covert security constraints which serves as digital evidence against external threats. The proposed approach offers enhanced security (i.e., stronger tamper tolerance and lower probability of coincidence) compared to prior works at negligible design cost overhead.

articleTitle: Integrating Traditional Culinary Techniques with Modern Technology: Power Tandoor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: The traditional clay tandoor oven, a cornerstone of South Asian and Middle Eastern cuisine, presents challenges for modern kitchens. While delivering a unique smoky flavor, its operation can be labor-intensive, require constant monitoring, and contribute to air pollution. Existing electric tandoors often struggle to replicate the authenticity of clay ovens, or their size and weight make them impractical for home use. We introduce the Power Tandoor, a novel electric tandoor design that addresses these limitations. The Power Tandoor leverages a traditional clay oven for authentic flavor while integrating innovative features for improved efficiency and user experience. An optimized lid design minimizes heat loss, and a microcontroller-based heating system allows for precise temperature control. This user-friendly design simplifies operation, making it ideal for diverse settings like home kitchens, restaurants, or dhabas. The Power Tandoor represents a significant advancement in tandoor technology, offering convenience, improved efficiency, precise temperature control, and the traditional tandoor flavor, all while prioritizing safety and environmental responsibility.

articleTitle: Side Channel Attack on 8051 Microcontroller
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: Launching a Power Analysis Side-Channel Attack (SCA) involving predicting the contents of a register within an 8051 (AT89S52) microcontroller. This prediction is made possible by repeatedly executing the same instruction with various data inputs and monitoring the power consumption patterns using an Oscilloscope. Power traces are analyzed using machine learning techniques to forecast the data after noise reduction. The underlying concept of this method is that a microcontroller's power usage is influenced by two factors: the operations being performed, and the data being processed. By keeping the instruction constant, any variation in power consumption is attributed solely to the differences in the data being handled.

articleTitle: Anomaly Detection from CCTV Camera Feed
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: The paper presents a novel approach for detecting anomalies like arson, explosion, vandalism, etc in public spaces using CCTV camera feeds. We propose a deep learning-based system that analyzes video streams to identify unusual events or behaviours that deviate from normal patterns. Our method combines Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) for feature extraction with Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks to model temporal dependencies in the video sequences. The system is trained on the UCF Crime Dataset to learn normal activity patterns and can flag potential anomalies in emulated real-time situations. To enhance accuracy, we incorporate additional computer vision technique, like optical flow, with CNN/SNN and LSTM to get various combinations of models (OF-CNN, OF-CNNLSTM, OF-SNN, OF-SNNLSTM, CNNLSTM) for improved anomaly detection. The proposed system has potential applications in enhancing public safety and security monitoring in urban environments.

articleTitle: LSTM Based Model Predictive Control Approach for Energy Management System in PV-Battery Integrated Microgrid Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: This paper proposes an intelligent energy management system in grid-connected microgrid with renewable energy and battery storage systems. The battery charging and discharging strategy is regulated so that the overall energy cost, along with battery degradation cost, is minimized considering the variation in grid tariff, inconsistent renewable power output and changing load demand. The proposed model is developed as an optimization-based problem over a 24-hour horizon using Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) based forecasting Energy Management-based Model Predictive Control. The proposed model provides information about the renewable power generation and demand for next 24 hours through LSTM based prediction model. The Long Short-Term Memory network is developed for time series forecasting of renewable generation and its performance is compared with other regression models. The Receding Horizon strategy is proposed to reduce the forecasting results of LSTM is fed as inputs to the Model Predictive Control based Energy management system forecasts and enable the implementation of energy management system. The proposed algorithm is developed and implemented in microgrid environment in MATLAB/Simulink 2022b under three case studies and the results claim that the proposed LSTM-MPC control strategy is successful in terms of reducing the grid consumption cost without much degrading the energy storage. The proposed model is also validated in 1kW microgrid hardware setup and promising results are obtained

articleTitle: Harnessing Knowledge-Distillation for Lightweight AI-Implementation on Resource-Constrained Device
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: Smart wearable devices benefit from lightweight deep neural networks (DNNs) with small silicon footprints for efficient real-time processing. While compression techniques are often applied to heavier models, achieving lightweight DNNs for wearable technology, particularly in real-time applications, has been underexplored. This work proposes a knowledge-distillation approach to derive a lightweight student model from a pre-trained teacher model, which maintains high performance. Tested on real-world ECG data, the student DNN achieves 89% classification accuracy, matching the teacher model, with a 93.12% memory reduction. Furthermore, deployment on resource-constrained devices like Coral TPU shows a 2 to 6.5-fold throughput improvement compared to other devices.

articleTitle: HLS driven Hybrid GA-PSO for Design Space Exploration of Optimal Palmprint Biometric based IP Watermark and Loop Unrolling Factor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel high level synthesis (HLS) based hybrid Genetic Algorithm-Particle Swarm Optimization (GA-PSO) framework for concurrent design space exploration (DSE) of optimal palmprint biometric based intellectual property (IP) watermark and optimal loop unrolling factor. The proposed approach is a hybrid exploration framework that merges GA process with specific utility attributes of PSO based DSE framework such as mutation, local and global best design solution concepts, which aids in escaping getting stuck at local minima. The proposed approach is capable of providing low-cost robust detective security countermeasure against threats of IP ownership abuse and IP piracy using IP seller's optimal palmprint biometric watermark. The comparison of the proposed approach with related works demonstrated optimal quality palmprint watermark in terms of lower probability of coincidence (watermark collision) and stronger tamper tolerance ability, at zero design cost overhead.

articleTitle: Secure Accelerated Computing: High-Level Synthesis Based Hardware Accelerator Design for CNN Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel methodology for designing secure hardware accelerator tailored for convolutional neural network (CNN) applications, leveraging security-aware high-level synthesis (HLS). The methodology outlined offers comprehensive security measures, including hindrance against reverse engineering (RE) and intellectual property (IP) piracy concerns through architectural transformations and embedded biometric palmprint constraints, respectively. Key contributions of this methodology include: i) robust hindrance against RE attack, ii) robust piracy detection with no additional design overhead, iii) definitive proof of IP ownership by achieving significantly lower probability of coincidence (P), indicating lower probability of false positive, and iv) enhanced tamper tolerance (TT) and resilience against brute force attacks compared to recent methodologies.

articleTitle: SecureHD: Designing Low-Cost Reliable and Security Aware Hardware Accelerators During High-Level Synthesis for Computationally Intensive Application Frameworks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: Reliable and low-cost hardware accelerator design and its security countermeasures are crucial to safeguard not only the end consumer but also the intellectual property (IP) vendor and system-on-chip (SoC) integrator. The reusable hardware accelerator-based design paradigm has become popular for its usage in several consumer electronics (CE) and computing systems. This is because the usage of hardware accelerators enables higher performance and efficacy by accelerating the underlying computationally-intensive application frameworks. In the proposed work, secure hardware accelerators for digital signal processing (DSP), multimedia and machine learning frameworks are designed (at zero design overhead) during high-level synthesis (HLS) as it offers lesser design complexity than lower levels of chip design. Further, HLS facilitates to integration of modules for design space exploration and integrating multi-layer security. The proposed methodologies offer the following: (a) hardware accelerator design for various computationally intensive application frameworks (b) negligible design cost overhead (c) seamless detective control against counterfeiting (d) higher tamper tolerance (e) low probability of false positive (f) higher strength of obfuscation to thwart reverse engineering attack.

articleTitle: Offline Power Estimation in CMOS VLSI Circuits Using Machine Learning Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: Accurate power estimation in CMOS VLSI circuits is vital for energy efficiency, performance optimization, and thermal management. This paper introduces a novel machine learning-based method for power estimation using a Random Forest model, with activity factor <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\alpha)$</tex> as a crucial parameter. We propose a method for predicting power consumption by analysing circuit parameters and power consumption reports. The prediction accuracy is validated by comparing simulated and predicted values. For internal and total power, an activity factor <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\alpha)$</tex> value of 0.1 yields better overall prediction accuracy compared to an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex> value of 0.4. Nevertheless, using the default <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex> value, the predicted values closely approximate the simulated results. Early power estimation is essential for design engineers to make informed decisions during the design phase, ensuring efficient power management and reliable circuit performance. Our ML-based approach achieves accuracy comparable to traditional techniques and enhances computational efficiency, providing a valuable tool for the design process.

articleTitle: Implementation and Analysis of Sparse DNN on GPU
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: Deep Neural Networks are being widely used in applications like object detection, image classification, etc. Having billions of parameters in the networks poses challenges in terms of storage requirements, and computational complexity. Exploiting sparsity in weights and input activations results in reduced memory and accelerated computations. This paper evaluates the performance of a sparse neural network inference on GPU that utilizes a clustering technique to convert the intermediate results into sparser representation during inference time with a sparse matrix storage format. The methodology utilizes Delta-Compressed Sparse Row sparse weight storage format for reduced memory requirements. The proposed approach has been implemented on NVIDIA Tesla T4 GPU, using medium-scale sparse DNN trained with MNIST dataset. Our implementation has achieved an average reduction of 4% in storage requirement and a maximum speedup of 1.92 × compared to baseline SNICIT implementation.

articleTitle: Open Source SoC Design for Low-Cost Micro Weather Station
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: This paper proposes a modular SoC, allowing for the dynamic addition or removal of peripherals such as I2C, UART, and other interfaces. Our current implementation targets a remote weather station as a case study, utilizing an Ibex core to interface with a BMP280 pressure sensor, an AHT10 temperature and humidity sensor, and an ESP8266 module for Wi-Fi connectivity to upload data to ThingSpeak for real-time monitoring. It also provides a contrast between collected data and regional data. The proposed SoC design enhances flexibility and cost-effectiveness by leveraging the open-source Ibex core, eliminating the need for paid licenses and toolchains. FPGA-based prototyping ensures robust verification and functional correctness of the designed SoC. The results demonstrate the potential of the proposed SoC platform for a wide range of embedded applications beyond environmental monitoring.

articleTitle: Power, Performance, and Area Optimisation of the RISC-V Processor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: RISc-V is a processor core designed according to an open standard instruction set architecture (ISA). Its architecture is important in the world of computing due to its scalable and customisable design., along with its precision. The processor finds its application across various domains., which presents complex challenges related to the tailored requirements of capabilities. In this paper., an endeavour has been made to optimise the power., performance., and area of the processor core by implementing design strategies to increase the clock frequency by 50% and reduce the die area by 3 %.

articleTitle: VLSI Architecture for the Phase Unwrapping Module in Contactless Vibration Sensing for Biomedical Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: Phase-unwrapping (PU) is a critical signal processing step used in fields such as radar, sonar, and laser technology. This paper presents a faster and more efficient VLSI architecture for implementing the phase-unwrapping algorithm on FPGA platforms. To evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed FPGA-based VLSI architecture for the phase-unwrapping algorithm in chest wall vibration sensing, we compared its performance with both a PYNQ board implementation and an equivalent software solution. The results are compared in terms of speed, resource utilization, and power consumption. Additionally, prototypes were developed on both the ZedBoard and PYNQ board, and the outcomes were physically verified. The proposed VLSI architecture achieves nearly 70 x and 111 x speed-up compared to software-based solutions and PYNQ board implementations, respectively.

articleTitle: Development of an AI based Edge Computing System for Malayalam Vowel Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: Malayalam language is characterized as a phone-mic language wherein graphemes are directly associated with phonemes. Malayalam words are essentially compositions of the phonetic units, the vowels and the consonants in the order they appear in the written script. Vowels exhibit distinctive waveforms that recur multiple times, contributing to the perception of a unique sound. This endeavor seeks to undertake a classification of Malayalam vowels utilizing an embedded platform, thereby facilitating analysis of the language's phonetic structure for the recognition of the Malayalam words.

articleTitle: A Method of Variable Frequency Clock Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: Dynamic Frequency Scaling (DFS) is a power management technique used in computing systems to adjust the frequency of a processor or other digital components based on workload demand thereby offering energy efficiency, thermal management, and performance tuning. Variable Frequency Clock (VFC) is one such form of DFS, where a slew of frequency is noted from minimum frequency <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(f_{min})$</tex> to maximum frequency <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(f_{max})$</tex>. Literature confirms a few approaches of VFC generation using mixed-signal circuit and digital circuits, where scope of improvement still exists in terms of attaining lower frequency ramp. Keeping that in mind, a new VFC architecture is unveiled in this paper with minimized effective slew rate and a controllable dynamic frequency slew rate. The implementation and functional verification of this work is carried out for UMC65nm CMOS on Cadence Virtuoso platform at a supply voltage (Vnn) of 1.1V.

articleTitle: SleepTrackSoC: Design and Implementation of Power and Cost Efficient Cortex-M0 based Sleep Tracking SoC
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: The design and implementation of system-on-chip (SoC) solutions for affordable, low-power, continuous sleep monitoring applications face challenges of complex design and high licensing cost of EDA tools required. To address such challenges, we propose SleepTrackSoC, a sleep tracking SoC platform that utilizes the ARM-Cortex-MO processor. The design functionality is verified by prototyping on the Basys 3 FPGA board. The RTL-to-GDSII flow for the proposed SoC is implemented entirely using open-source EDA tools (OpenLane). We leverage OpenLane and low silicon footprint of Cortex-MO in the proposed platform to reduce the cost and power respectively, making it suitable for wearable applications. We optimise the area of final physical design to 2.47 mm2 at a clock frequency of 5 MHz consuming total 175 μ W of power at typical corner, using meticulous floorplanning and macro-placement, and performing various size-offs to make it fabrication ready.

articleTitle: A Reconfigurable Floating-Point Compliant Hardware Architecture for Neural Network Implementation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: Neural network architectures are increasingly pop-ular for their ability to perform fast and efficient compu-tations, leveraging inherent parallelism for quicker operation than conventional sequential methods. This paper presents a novel reconfigurable neural network architecture implemented with computationally less intensive hardware, along with a hardware accelerator-based design of a feed-forward neural network. The primary aim of this work is to optimize power and area utilization metrics using an approximate computing paradigm and a control unit that synchronizes the forward and backward passes. Moreover, in this paper, we introduce a compact and scalable hardware design approach for neural networks, validated through simulations and implementations on Xilinx Zynq and Zynq UltraScale+ MPSoC FPGA boards. Our architecture significantly reduces area overhead by 2.58 %, enhances power efficiency with an average power consumption of 110.67 mW, and achieves a 4.68-fold increase in throughput compared to software implementations. This improvement, while maintaining an average accuracy of around 91 % across different architectures, is due to the use of reconfigurable features and Padé-based optimization techniques.

articleTitle: Plant Disease Detection in Smart Agriculture: A Power-aware Edge-AI Implementation on Cortex-A53
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: The need for highly optimal farming practices is justified by the scarcity of natural resources, increased cost incurred due to diseased yield, and lower quantity and quality of production due to lack of informed fertilizer usage on cultivation lands. Each facet, particularly early disease detection and reactive remediation, constitutes the foundation on which an agricultural ecosystem relies. We have thus proposed a low-cost, power-efficient system that calibrates real-time, on-field information and collaborates with weather data and disease databases to leverage the early class estimation of diseases and risk factor analysis. The system is designed on a sensor-integrated, Cortex-A53 Raspberry Pi 3 platform that performs plant disease detection using low-cost, high-accuracy CNN architectures. The System design is facilitated by non-obtrusive On-field and User-end systems, which ensures lower communication bandwidth, efficient memory consumption, environmental adaptability, and reduced power utilization. A centralized database that facilitates information storage and retrieval, enabling updation in both the operating functional components, allows for an incremental learning paradigm that can extensively cater to local characteristics and feature-scope for the system. This allows more excellent run-time performance regarding accuracy and resource utilization, enhancing sustainability and ease of deployment.

articleTitle: SPEEDNet: Salient Pyramidal Enhancement Encoder-Decoder Network for Colonoscopy Images
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: Accurate identification and precise delineation of regions of significance, such as tumors or lesions, is a pivotal goal in medical imaging analysis. This paper proposes SPEEDNet, a novel architecture for precisely segmenting lesions within colonoscopy images. SPEEDNet uses a novel block named “Dilated-Involutional Pyramidal Convolution Fusion” (DIPC). A DIPC block combines the dilated involution layers pairwise into a pyramidal structure to convert the feature maps into a compact space. This design lowers the total number of parameters while improving the learning of representations across an optimal receptive field. The proposed DIPC Block prioritizes the integration of salient maps and feature maps from the preceding stage of the encoder through a direct feed-forward connection. We have employed Tversky Loss to handle the class imbalance challenge and manage the trade-off between precision and recall. On the EBHISeg dataset, SPEEDNet outperforms five state-of-art networks, viz., UNet, FeedNet, SegNet, MedT and AttesResDUNet. Precisely, SPEEDNet attains an average dice score of 0.952 and a recall of 0.971. Qualitative results and ablation studies provide additional insights into the effectiveness of SPEEDNet. The model size of SPEEDNet is 9.8 MB, significantly smaller than that of UNet (119.8 MB), FeedNet (61.8 MB), and AttesResDUNet (139.1 MB). SPEEDNet has a throughput of 33 frames per second on the GeForce MX330 GPU.

articleTitle: Mender-FPGA: An Open Source Framework for FPGA Remote Update for ML Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: The last decade has seen a massive adoption of FPGA devices in various fields like electronics, robotics, machine vision, etc. Over-the-Air (OTA) updates are becoming an important feature for internet-connected intelligent embedded devices. Such remote updates offer flexibility in updating an existing system remotely without physical access to it. The intelligence-based embedded devices' software modules (like AI/ML models) may need to be updated frequently. The traditional approach to update Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) uses JTAG programming, which is limited to wired connectivity with 5 to 10 devices. However, when these FPGA devices are deployed at a remote location, the need for automatic wireless or wired updates increases over manual updates. In this paper, we discuss the design and implementation of an open-source framework for over-the-air and remote wired update for SoC FPGA devices using the open-source Mender platform. We specifically address two features: (1) full system update, (2) delta-update to update the FPGA functionality similar to full software updates and software patches respectively, and include a rollback mechanism for device recovery. We implemented and tested all the above features on Zed board to demonstrate the proposed approach and framework for machine learning applications on such devices. Our result shows the successful implementation of the remote update method for FPGAs and is the first to develop an open-source framework targeting Zed board.

articleTitle: rA*: Re-Planned A* Technique for Point-to-Point Robot Navigation in Dynamic Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: Autonomous point-to-point robots employ path-finding algorithms to traverse from the start to the goal point by avoiding obstacles. One such prominent and efficient algorithm is A*. It uses the best first technique to traverse a particular environment and extract the shortest path by avoiding on-path obstacles. It is widely accepted for its optimality in finding the shortest path from one node to another. In the case of real-world scenarios, robot navigation involves dynamic obstacles with varying costs and multiple objectives. This paper proposes the rA* (replanned A*) technique, which implements important modifications to the A* algorithm to address the challenges created in dynamic environments by introducing dynamic cost adjustment with sensor data to reduce path distance in replanning in case of obstacles or complex terrain features differences in an environment. We also enhance the heuristic approach with environmental awareness by equipping Euclidean distance for faster navigation. Real-time and multi-objective path planning have been conceptualized to dynamically adjust path in case of moving obstacles. Real-time analysis of the algorithm is conducted on a Turtlebot by taking the sensor-fused input data in coordinate and depth format. The sensor data is obtained through ROS (Robot Operating System) visualizer and the map of the path exploration by detecting the dynamic obstacles is generated through G-mapping. The maps are fed as input to the rA* algorithm to re-plan the path, distorted by the sudden appearance of dynamic obstacles. rA* reduces the overall and near-obstacles turning angle of the robot by 80.4% - 82.2%, as compared to the traditional A* technique. The results prove rA* to be superseded in terms of accurate path tracking and control by precise obstacle avoidance and achieving intelligent navigation.

articleTitle: Power Conscious Asynchronous FIFO for Forest Event Surveillance
