publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: Asynchronous First-In-First-Out (FIFO) structures play a crucial role in real-time data processing systems, particularly in applications like forest event surveillance, where power efficiency is paramount. This paper presents designing and implementing a power-conscious clock-gated asynchronous FIFO tailored for forest event monitoring systems. The proposed FIFO architecture exploits asynchronous communication to reduce power consumption. We suggest leveraging the clock gating technique at the RTL level to dynamically disable clock signals in idle or non-operational periods of the FIFO, thereby reducing unnecessary power consumption. Additionally, optimization in synthesis level design makes the scheme achieve notable reductions in dynamic power consumption of 25% and leakage power reduction of 1.16%, with compensation of 0.46% increase in total area, while maintaining performance and functionality requirements.

articleTitle: HLS Based Rapid Pareto Front Search of Watermarked Convolutional Layer IP Design
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: This paper presents a novel methodology for high level synthesis (HLS) based Pareto front search of watermarked convolutional layer intellectual property (IP) designs. The presented exploration framework is rapidly capable of pruning the design space of watermarked IP designs using a combination of architecture tree configuration and dominance factor logic. Experimental results validate that the proposed approach is capable of providing significant speedup in the exploration time compared to exhaustive analysis. Further, results of security analysis in terms of watermark robustness achieved by the proposed approach against standard attacks of false ownership claim, tampering and watermark collision have also been reported.

articleTitle: Stress Detection and Monitoring: A Systematic Review
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: Stress and depression management has become one of the major global challenges in the context of the mental health of youth and the working class, as well as the healthier aging of older ones today. This article briefly reviews techniques for detecting human stress based on relevant features/biomarkers. It reviews the state-of-the-art, identifies relevant features/biomarkers, and establishes their relation to stress. The determined and presented features related to stress detection here include salivary cortisol, EEG, MR-GR balance, and GSR. All these features can be measured from the head region, viz., the head surface, forehead, and mouth of a human body. These features can be fed into any Intelligent expert system to automate the decision process with proper, accurate modeling. A proposal for such an intelligent expert system has been presented in this paper.

articleTitle: Gen-Sign: HLS Based Watermarking Using IP Vendor's Feistel Cipher Encrypted Genomic Signature for Protecting CNN and Image Processing Filter Cores Against Piracy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: This paper presents a novel hardware intellectual property (IP) watermarking process during high level synthesis (HLS) that leverages IP vendor human body sample in the form of genomic sequence to act as secret invisible encrypted signature (called 'Gen-Sign‘), The proposed encrypted genomic signature is used as an imperceptible watermark to secure convolutional neural network (CNN) and image processing filter against IP piracy. The presented approach has been evaluated on benchmarks in terms of design cost overhead, probability of coincidence, tamper tolerance and entropy. Results of the proposed approach indicate superior security at 0% design overhead, compared to prior approaches.

articleTitle: A Stacking Ensemble Technique to Predict Speed and Distance in 4G and 5G Communication Datasets
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: Understanding the circumstances and behavior of mobile users can significantly enhance the intelligence of mobile networks. Distance and speed of users constitute crucial components of the user profile. For example, predicting the user's speed can allow these networks to perform better resource allocation and identify high user-density areas and handover trends. We leverage machine learning to predict the user's speed and distance. Based on user behaviors, we define various User Equipment (UE) speed (or distance) categories, each including a range of speed values. We evaluate both solo machine learning (ML) algorithms and a stacking ensemble ML algorithm. We observe that the stacking-based ensemble algorithm, consisting of a decision tree and random forest classifier, provides the best accuracy. We evaluate our technique on three datasets viz., 4G-Passive, 5G-Passive, and 5G-Coverage. For speed prediction on 4G passive, 5G passive, and 5G coverage datasets, the accuracy values are 66.2 %, 88.7%, and 93.4 %, respectively. For distance prediction on the 4G passive dataset, the accuracy is 90.9 %. Our work demonstrates that it is possible to accurately profile the range of speed and distance using real-world, contextual data collected from 4G and 5G network deployments.

articleTitle: VATML: Towards On Device Ventricular Arrhythmia Detection Using TinyML
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: Cardiac arrhythmias pose a significant health risk, underscoring the critical need for precise detection. This paper introduces “VATML: Ventricular Arrhythmia Detection using TinyML” demonstrating TinyML's potential to enable detection within implantable cardioverter defibrillators (ICDs), a common medical device. TinyML i.e. deploying machine learning on resource-constrained edge devices, holds promise for healthcare transformation. VATML features a lightweight 1D Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), tailored for life-threatening Ventricular Arrhythmias (VAs), with a minimal 17.33 KiB memory footprint and low Multiply-Accumulate (MAC) complexity of 11.51K, meeting ICD operational demands. Experimental results showcase VATML's notable performance, achieving a high <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{F}_{1}$</tex> score of 98.33 % and a generalization score of 93.75 % on the STM32F303K8 board with an ARM Cortex-M4 processor compared to competing methods.

articleTitle: Message from the General Chairs: iSES 2024
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: It is our privilege to welcome all the participants to the vibrant and colorful city of New Delhi, India. We warmly welcome you to the 1Oth IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (IEEE-iSES, formerly I EEE-iNIS, https://www.ieee-ises.org/). The primary objective of I EEE-iSES is to provide a platform for hardware, software, and system researchers to interact under one umbrella to catalyze the future development of smart electronic systems. Efficient VLSI-driven circuits, sensors, and architectures are at the heart of modern electronic systems. At the same time, efficient artificial intelligence and machine learning algorithms, firmware, and middleware complement the hardware to enable adaptable softwaredriven strategies for efficient processing, communication, and storage in our digital world. These foundational hardware and software components are the driving force behind emerging Internet of Things (loT) devices, edge computing, cyber-physical systems, and large cloud computing platforms. The growth and proliferation of these platforms is largely dependent upon advances in both hardware and software. Disseminating and promoting such advances is a key goal of IEEE-iSES.

publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: It is a great pleasure for us to welcome you to the 1 01h IEEE International Symposium on SmartElectronic Systems (IEEE iSES, https://ieee-ises.org) in New Delhi, the capital city of India. The symposiumaddresses key technologies and enabling technologies for Smart Systems as well as solutions forenergy, agriculture, health, biomedical, industry, housing, sustainability, social cohesion, andmobility. Smart systems entail architectures, systems software, and algorithms as key technologies.Nonetheless, other technologies such as the internet, data analytics, security, and cognitive sciencejoin as enabling technologies.
